about.title: Vallejo Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A product that fails without warning can turn an ordinary day in Vallejo upside down. Maybe a space heater in a home off Tennessee Street shorted out, a power tool jammed mid-cut, or a car seat did not hold the way the box said it would. California law gives Solano County residents a clear path: under strict liability, you generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. You need to show the product had a defect — in its design, in how that particular unit was made, or in the warnings that came with it — and that the defect caused your injury. That also widens who can be held responsible, since the maker, the distributor, and the store that sold it may each share liability. Vallejo's 2025 public records list 439 injury collisions and 610 people hurt; some crashes on I-80, Sonoma Boulevard, or Broadway Street involve a tire, brake, or airbag that did not perform as designed, and those can be product cases too. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm; the independent attorneys we match you with work on contingency.

items.title: Strict Liability, Explained Plainly
items.desc: Attorneys in our network know that a California product claim usually turns on proving a defect and causation, not the manufacturer's state of mind. That focus shapes how your case is investigated from the first call.

items.title: Help Preserving the Evidence
items.desc: The product itself is often the heart of the case. An attorney can advise you right away on keeping the item, its packaging, and receipts intact instead of returning or discarding them.

items.title: Every Link in the Chain
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers may all be liable under California law. The attorney we connect you with can identify each responsible party, which matters when a maker is overseas or hard to reach.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company was negligent to win a product liability case in California?
items.answer: Usually not. California applies strict liability to most product claims, which means you generally need to show the product was defective in design, manufacturing, or warnings and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the company was careful is often beside the point. An attorney can explain which theory fits your situation.

items.question: I was in a crash on I-80 near Vallejo and I think my airbag never deployed. Is that a product claim?
items.answer: It might be. If a safety component such as an airbag, seatbelt, tire, or brake failed to perform as designed, the vehicle or part maker may be liable in addition to any driver at fault. Keep the vehicle from being scrapped or repaired until an attorney can arrange an inspection, since the car itself is key evidence.

items.question: I threw away the product that hurt me. Can I still do anything?
items.answer: You may still have options, but the case becomes harder. Photos, purchase records, the packaging, medical notes describing the injury, and recall notices can help fill in gaps. Talk with an attorney soon so remaining evidence can be gathered before it disappears.
